cards.design_implication: If the research involves studying protein LLPS, experimental designs should consider measuring or controlling variables related to electrostatic, hydrophobic, and H-bonding interactions to assess their specific contributions to phase formation.
does_not_establish: The exact quantitative weights of each interaction type for every protein.
Generalizability to all proteins or polypeptides outside the studied set.
Specific experimental conditions or measurement techniques used to determine the role of these interactions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We further demonstrated that electrostatic, hydrophobic, and H-bonding or a combination of such intermolecular interactions plays a crucial role in individual protein/peptide LLPS.
limitations: The claim is limited to the specific proteins and polypeptides studied in this work (a total of 23).
As an abstract, it does not provide the quantitative data or detailed experimental methods used to distinguish the relative contributions of each interaction type.
cards.statement: Electrostatic, hydrophobic, and H-bonding interactions, or combinations thereof, are proposed to play a crucial role in the liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of individual proteins and peptides.

cards.design_implication: When selecting candidates for LLPS investigation, proteins or domains known to be intrinsically disordered or unstructured may be prioritized as they are hypothesized to facilitate the multivalent interactions necessary for phase separation.
does_not_establish: That all unstructured domains undergo LLPS.
The specific mechanism by which multivalent interactions occur in this study.
A causal link established by the experimental results of this specific paper for this general background fact.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Unstructured and intrinsically disordered domains are known to facilitate multivalent interactions driving protein LLPS.
limitations: This statement reflects background knowledge or established context cited within the abstract rather than a new finding from this specific study.
It does not specify which types of unstructured domains were effective in this particular experiment.
cards.statement: Intrinsically disordered and unstructured domains are known to facilitate multivalent interactions that drive protein LLPS.
